The authorization-server metadata advertises authorization-code, refresh-token and client-credentials grants; S256 PKCE; client registration; and token endpoint authentication methods none, client_secret_post and client_secret_basic. No scopes_supported value appears in the supplied metadata. Token lifetime and revocation are not specified there.

The supplied protected-resource documents identify https://mcp.mtnewswires.com as authorization server, bearer via header, and https://mcp.mtnewswires.com/mcp as resource. D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The seven official tools are news search/retrieval, category listing and formatting. Their operations appear read-oriented; official tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) are not published. 2. No server-enforced confirmation, preview/confirm flow or MCP elicitation is documented. Tool approval is described as a client setting. 3. OAuth metadata supports bearer authorization but lists no scopes_supported. Product-role inheritance, admin switches beyond ChatGPT workspace enablement, allowlists, redirect approval, token lifetime and revocation are not documented. 4. No read-only mode, tool filters, URL flags, environment separation or regional endpoint is documented. 5. No tool-level masking or content boundary logic is documented. Privacy material says prompts and tool request/response payloads are collected; it advises users not to include sensitive personal information. 6. Individual subscription article limits are 3,500/week or 10,000/week, with one-month or one-year rolling histories; enterprise is listed as having no article-volume limits. Per-call rate limits, bulk caps and result truncation are not documented. 7. Input validation, coercion, unknown-argument handling and operator overrides are not documented; schemas are unpublished. 8. The vendor says it collects prompts (unless opted out), request parameters, response payloads and tool-call metadata for abuse prevention, diagnosis and quality/relevance improvements. Prompts and tool-call payloads may be retained up to one year; billing data at least one year. Prompt collection opt-out is by email and takes effect within five business days; deletion requests are completed within 30 days. 9. No feedback/rating/report/survey tool or tool-result upsell is documented. Paid subscription tiers are presented on the signup page. 10. No server-provided behavioral instructions or skills are documented; the official tool descriptions are brief summaries. 11. No agent-behavior memory or state feature is documented. 12. The input is one global hosted MCP endpoint; no proxy/subserver hierarchy is documented. 13. No raw API, arbitrary query, SQL, script or execution escape-hatch tool appears in the official list.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The vendor recommends client-side convenience settings: “set its access to 'Always allow'” for Claude, and “Allow read actions with no user confirmation” for ChatGPT. These instructions describe client configuration, not a server-enforced approval or safety mechanism. The vendor also says: “We recommend not including sensitive personal information in your queries.”
F_documentation.governance_promises: The vendor says prompt and tool-call payloads are retained “for up to 1 year,” and that aggregate non-identifying statistics “may be retained longer.” It states: “We do not use this data to train generative models, and we do not share it with third-party model providers.” Prompt collection can be opted out by email; prompts and tool-call data may be deleted on request within 30 days. It says communications are encrypted using industry-standard TLS. These are vendor policy statements, not implementation details verified in public code.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The vendor describes licensed, permissioned access to real-time financial news, structured machine-readable content and integrations in AI clients. Its individual subscriptions specify weekly article/headline limits and rolling history periods; Enterprise is described as having no article-volume limits and negotiated history. Subscriber terms disclaim guarantees of accuracy, completeness, timeliness or reliability and state that the content is not investment advice.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The supplied OAuth metadata verifies protected-resource discovery and advertised authorization flows, but lists no OAuth scopes and does not reveal product entitlement enforcement. Public code was not found, so policy statements about collection, retention, access, deletion, TLS and model training could not be checked against implementation. Client confirmation advice is expressly client-side. Tool schemas and server annotations are unpublished.

contradictions: The vendor's official tool list names fetch_news and does not name onboarding. Anthropic's connector directory lists onboarding and omits fetch_news; Manufact and mcp.so show the same substitution. This analysis retains all seven official names and adds onboarding as a third-party catalogue-only name.

An older statement captured in the Agentman catalogue says MT Newswires stores no user-generated content, including prompts and request/response bodies. The vendor's current MCP documentation states that, as of October 15, 2026, it collects prompts unless users opt out and retains tool-call request and response payloads for up to one year. The vendor page is used as the current policy evidence.

Agentman reports Anthropic's directory as “Read and write,” while the listed tool names and vendor descriptions indicate search, retrieval, listing and formatting operations. The directory's classification is inconsistent with the published operation descriptions.
observations_for_research: The official web documentation recommends client-side options that reduce confirmation prompts for read actions; the OAuth metadata itself advertises no scopes_supported field.
The vendor's current privacy page describes collection of prompts and tool-call payloads with opt-out and deletion request paths, alongside tool-call metadata and billing records.
Official and catalogue tool lists differ by one name: the official list has fetch_news, while several catalogues show onboarding.
notes: Reviewed links.json, links_check.txt, all listed page text/HTML/script extracts, and the local code directory; no vendor repository or package copy was present.
